Render a parsed $PK expression node as R source

nmDeparse.Rd

Turns one expression node from the statements tree of nmParsePK() into a string of R code. THETA(n) becomes <thetaVar>[n] and every ETA(n) becomes the literal text etaValue ("0" gives typical values). Symbols and covariate names are emitted unchanged, ** becomes ^, and parentheses are added only where operator precedence needs them.

Usage

nmDeparse(node, thetaVar = "thetas", etaValue = "0", epsValue = "0")

Arguments

node

An expression node - a rhs or cond from an nmParsePK() statement, or a sub-node of one.

thetaVar

Name of the vector that THETA(n) indexes into. Default "thetas".

etaValue

Text substituted for every ETA(n). Default "0". Pass, for example, "eta[3]" to keep the random effect.

epsValue

Text substituted for every EPS(n)/ERR(n), which only a $PRED block can contain. Default "0", so the residual error drops out of a typical-value function exactly as ETA(n) does.

Value

A length-one character string of R source.

See also

nmParsePK().

Examples

modFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/run7.mod", package = "PMXForest")
p <- nmParsePK(modFile)
#> Warning: The reference value for GENO1, GENO3 was inferred rather than read from the control stream. Check the preamble of the generated function and override through covRef if it is wrong.
# render the right-hand side of the first assignment
first <- Find(function(s) s$type == "assign", p$statements)
nmDeparse(first$rhs, thetaVar = "thetas")
#> [1] "FRELFORM * FRELGENO4 * FRELSEX"
